songInfo.title: Ain't Talkin' 'bout Love
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C - D - E - F - G
scalesUsed.application: Drives the somber yet ferocious main arpeggio sequence and chord changes (Am - F - G)
The bedrock for Eddie's aggressive blues-rock fills, wide finger vibrato, and screaming pinch harmonics

scalesUsed.notes: A - C - D - Eb - E - G
scalesUsed.application: The flatted 5th (Eb) injects quintessential Sunset Strip grit and sleazy chromatic swagger

keyAndScale.keySignature: No sharps or flats (concert Ab minor due to half-step down tuning)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A Minor is the relative minor of C Major

mainProgression.description: One of the most instantly recognizable guitar riffs in hard rock history. Eddie arpeggiates open A minor, moving to an innovative thumb-over F major voicing, then sliding to G major with aggressive palm-muted pick attack.

sectionProgressions.description: Crisp palm-muted arpeggios electrified by an MXR Flanger and Echoplex tape delay
Continuous arpeggiated drive punctuated by low E string chugging and percussive pick scratches
Massive unmuted power chords ringing with high harmonic overtone drive and energetic vocal backing
Ascending modal staircase that builds palpable energy before dropping back to the stripped-down bass and guitar intro motif

harmonicFunction: Am (i) - Heavy, resonant tonic minor chord anchoring the punk-rock aggression
F (bVI) - Submediant chord providing emotional depth and classic minor modal tension
G (bVII) - Subtonic chord providing high-velocity forward momentum back to the tonic

techniques.name: Precision Palm-Muted Arpeggiation
techniques.description: Resting the edge of the pick-hand palm lightly against the bridge saddles while picking arpeggiated single notes with percussive attack, creating punchy definition that cuts through heavy Marshall gain

notes: Apply firm yet light palm pressure directly over the bridge saddles
Do not press too hard or notes will go sharp and lose pitch resonance
Maintain strict down-up-down alternate picking across strings 5, 4, 3, and 2
Accentuate the open A string pedal notes on beat 1 of each cycle
sequence: Pick open A 5th string downbeat with strong palm mute
Pick fret 2 on D string, fret 2 on G string, and fret 1 on B string in ascending order
Shift fret hand quickly to F voicing (fret 1 on low E string with thumb or index)
Slide up to G (fret 3 on low E string) with aggressive pick snap
tips: Use a heavy plectrum (1.0mm+) to ensure maximum percussive click against the strings
Keep the pickup selector on the bridge humbucker with amp mids boosted
Engage a flanger pedal with slow sweep to reproduce Eddie's authentic 1978 studio shimmer

techniques.name: Screaming Pinch Harmonics & Tremolo Flutter
techniques.description: Grazing the picked string with the edge of the pick-hand thumb immediately upon striking to excite screaming artificial overtones, coupled with subtle vintage vibrato arm manipulation

notes: Hold the pick with minimal tip exposed (1-2mm)
Strike the string firmly while allowing the fleshy side of the thumb to brush the string simultaneously
Target specific nodal points roughly 3 to 5 inches above the bridge pickup
Add immediate, wide wrist vibrato once the harmonic blooms to sustain the scream
sequence: Fret note on string 3 (e.g., fret 7 or 9)
Dig pick into the string with glancing thumb follow-through
Listen for the whistling octave or fifth harmonic overtone
Dip and flutter the vibrato bar lightly for classic EVH shimmer
tips: A hot bridge humbucker and moderate tube overdrive are essential to catch pinch harmonics easily
Experiment with moving your pick hand millimeter by millimeter along the string to find harmonic sweet spots
Never squeeze the neck too tightly with the fret hand during vibrato

sections.name: Intro Signature Arpeggio Riff
sections.description: One of rock's most electrifying openings: clean, staccato palm-muted arpeggios through an MXR Flanger building unstoppable momentum before the drums explode in.
notes: Heavy palm muting on strings 5, 4, and 3
Let the open notes ring with tight percussive definition
Smooth fret-hand transition between Am and thumb-over F
Lock strictly into 139 BPM pulse

sections.name: Verse 1 Punk-Rock Drive
sections.description: David Lee Roth's gritty vocals enter over Eddie's driving rhythm, punctuated by percussive pick slides and pick-hand slaps.
notes: Maintain steady palm muting behind the vocal phrases
Throw in ghost-note pick scratches on beat 4
Add subtle dynamic swell on the G major chord going into verse turns
Keep fret hand relaxed to prevent forearm cramp

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Explosion
sections.description: 'Ain't talkin' 'bout love! My love is rotten to the core!' - huge, unmuted power chords shake the arena with anthemic backing vocals.
notes: Release palm muting for massive full-body chord resonance
Strike A5, G5, and F5 power chords with aggressive downstrokes
Add high E and B string open drone over the G chord
Sharp snap back to palm muting on the riff return

sections.name: Guitar Solo & Sitar-Infused Melody
sections.description: Eddie plays a surprisingly melodic, lyrical solo (originally composed on a Danelectro electric sitar in the studio), featuring soaring blues bends and crying sustain.
notes: Singing full-step bends on fret 9 of the G string up to E
Wide, dramatic vibrato executed from the wrist
Incorporate subtle pinch harmonics on sustained notes
Rhythmic eighth-note repetitions creating hypnotic melodic tension

sections.name: Bridge Ascending Staircase
sections.description: 'You know you're semi-good lookin'...' - an energetic ascending chord climb over Am, Bm, C, and D building peak suspense.
notes: Stepwise ascending power chords on the 5th string
Syncopated sixteenth-note rhythm stabs
Heavy drum fills support the dynamic rise
Explosive pick slide dropping back into the main riff

sections.name: Outro Climax & Tremolo Flutter Jam
sections.description: High-octane outro repeating the signature riff with Eddie laying down incendiary pinch harmonics, dive bombs, and screaming feedback before the sudden hard stop.
notes: Dig hard into pinch harmonics over fret 5 of G and B strings
Depress the whammy bar for dramatic sub-octave dives
Keep the rhythm section locked at 139 BPM
Crisp unison stop on the final low A hit
sections.exerciseLabel: Outro Pinch Harmonics & Whammy Dive Jam

guitar.recommended: Frankenstrat or Superstrat with vintage PAF bridge humbucker
guitar.pickup: Hot bridge humbucker mounted directly into the body wood for explosive resonance

amp.recommended: 1968 Marshall 100W Super Lead (Model 1959) run through a Variac at ~90V

effects.distortion: Brown sound tube saturation from cranked Marshall power amp
effects.reverb: Subtle studio room reverb (Sunset Sound echo chamber)
effects.other: MXR Flanger (manual 11:00, width 2:00, speed 10:00, regen 2:00) and Echoplex EP-3 tape delay

beginner.title: Power Chords & Basic Progression
steps: Tune your guitar half-step down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Learn A5, F5, and G5 power chord shapes
Practice transitioning between the three chords in tempo at 139 BPM

intermediate.title: The Palm-Muted Signature Arpeggios
steps: Master the palm-muting technique on the lower strings
Practice the strict down-up alternate picking pattern cleanly
Learn the thumb-over F chord voicing for fluid transitions

advanced.title: Solo Phrasing, Pinch Harmonics & Whammy Work
steps: Transcribe and perform Eddie's melodic guitar solo note-for-note
Nail repeatable pinch harmonics across the G and B strings
Integrate subtle tremolo bar flutters and dive bombs seamlessly

commonMistakes: Pressing too hard with the pick-hand palm, completely choking note pitch instead of muting percussively
Playing in standard E tuning instead of tuning down one half-step (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Rushing the syncopation on the F-to-G transition
Neglecting alternate picking on the arpeggiated riff, causing pick-hand fatigue
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Half-step down open chord tuning check and finger warm-up
10 mins: Slow palm-muting arpeggio repetition at 90, 115, and 139 BPM
10 mins: Pinch harmonic accuracy drills over frets 5, 7, and 9
10 mins: Full rhythm play-through focusing on explosive chorus transitions
focusAreas: Bridge palm-muting pressure and sweet spot discovery
Alternate picking synchronization on string crosses
Authentic EVH vibrato and harmonic overtones
metronomeWork: Set the metronome at 90 BPM to lock in the palm-muted arpeggios perfectly
Increase tempo in 5 BPM steps once 4 consecutive flawless cycles are played
Practice muting all strings immediately on sudden rhythmic stops

sameArtist.title: Eruption
sameArtist.similarity: Showcases Eddie Van Halen's revolutionary two-handed tapping, tremolo picking, and brown sound
